Although this possibility is correct in meaning, the context of the speech does not indicate it. Rather, the certain and correct interpretation is the first one, for two reasons: first, because He restricted it by the time, which is the Day of Resurrection; and second, because the purpose here is to explain the condition of the people of the Fire in general, while that possibility concerns only a small part of them. Rather, the certain and correct interpretation is the first one, for two reasons: first, because He restricted it by the time, which is the Day of Resurrection; and second, because the purpose here is to explain the condition of the people of the Fire in general, while that possibility concerns only a small part of them. Moreover, the discussion concerns the state of people when the Overwhelming Event comes, so there is no reference here to their states in this world.

As for His saying {They will be exposed to a scorching Fire}: that is, its heat will be intense, surrounding them from every direction. {They will be given drink from a boiling spring} — that is, its heat is extreme. {If they ask for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces.} This is their drink. As for their food: {They will have no food except from a thorny plant, which neither nourishes nor satisfies hunger.} This is because the purpose of food is one of two things: either it satisfies the hunger of its eater and removes his pain, or it fattens his body from emaciation. This food has none of these two qualities; rather, it is food of extreme bitterness, foulness and vileness. We ask Allah for well-being.

{8–16} As for the people of goodness, their faces on the Day of Resurrection will be {joyful}, that is, the radiance of bliss will have come upon them, their bodies will be made radiant, their faces will shine, and they will be extremely happy, {pleased with their striving} — that is, with the righteous deeds and kindness to the servants of Allah that they had sent forward in this world, {in a lofty Garden} — that is, one that comprises all kinds of bliss, and is lofty in its place and its dwellings: its place is in the highest ʿIlliyyīn, and its dwellings are lofty homes, having upper chambers, and above the chambers are built chambers from which they overlook what Allah has prepared for them of honor. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 88, verses 17–26:

{17–20} Almighty God says, urging those who do not believe the Messenger (ﷺ), and other people as well, to reflect upon the creation of God, which points to His oneness: {Do they not look at the camels, how they have been created?}; that is: do they not look at their wondrous creation, and how God subjected them to the servants and made them submissive for their many benefits, upon which they depend? {And at the mountains, how they have been raised up?}: in a striking form by which the earth gained stability and was secured against turbulence, and in which God deposited the great benefits that He deposited. {And at the earth, how it has been spread out?}; that is: it has been extended to a wide expanse and made easy to traverse to the utmost degree, so that the servants may settle upon its surface, be able to till it, plant it, build upon it, and travel its paths.

Know that its being spread out does not contradict that it is a round sphere surrounded by the celestial spheres on all sides, as attested by transmission, reason, the senses and observation, as is mentioned and well known among many people, especially in these times, when people have come to know most of its regions through the means God has given them for bringing the distant near. The leveling only contradicts the roundness of a very small body, which, if it were flattened, would no longer have any noticeable curvature. As for the body of the earth, which is very large and vast, it is round yet flat-seeming, and the two matters do not conflict, as those with expertise know.

{21–22} {So remind, you are only a reminder}; that is: remind people, admonish them, warn them, and give them good tidings; for you have been sent to call creation to God and to remind them. You were not sent to be a overseer over them, empowered to control them and charged with their deeds. So when you have done what is incumbent upon you, there is no blame upon you afterwards; as in His saying, exalted is He: {And you are not over them a compeller. So remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My warning}.

{23–24} His saying: {Except he who turns away and disbelieves}; that is: but whoever turns away from obedience and disbelieves in God, {God will punish him with the greatest punishment}; that is: the severe and everlasting one.

{25–26} {Indeed, to Us is their return}; that is: the return of creation and their gathering on the Day of Resurrection. {Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning}: for what they did of good and evil.

And praise be to God [Lord of the worlds].
